summary: Current source already contains two-stage split-KV flash decoding. Direct MI350X measurements at the reported Llama GQA shape were 60.7 us at context 200 and 68.4 us at 2,000; forcing one split was 126.6 us at 2,000 and degraded to 2,031.8 us at 32,768 versus 115.6 us with scheduled splitting. No additional kernel optimization was justified.

tests.what_was_measured: Direct prepared Triton decode-attention latency, scheduler split counts, single-split control latency, finiteness, and correctness versus an independent float32 PyTorch reference for ten GQA/MHA, batch, long-context, gathered-index, heterogeneous-length, and masked-boundary cases on MI350X.
Repository correctness coverage for the normal MHA and grouped GQA Triton decode paths; 2 tests passed.

gpu_execution_evidence: AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950, ROCm 7.2, torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2. Raw timings and numerical errors are in decode_attention_results.json; generated stage-1/stage-2 gfx950 AMDGCN paths and hashes are in compiler_artifacts.txt.
remaining_limitations: No gated Llama-3.1-8B weights or end-to-end serving throughput run; direct kernel results isolate decode attention.
No FlashInfer comparison and no access to the report's original NVIDIA hardware.
The newer Qwen3.5/speculative-serving report uses different architecture and workload shapes and remains unverified here.
No native/FlyDSL code was involved, so no native rebuild was applicable.
